report.root_cause: The on-disk data for chunk (1,0) in world/region/r.0.0.mca was corrupt: its compressed payload failed to decompress (zlib "incorrect header check"). When the server restarted at about 07:33:35, Paper hit a ZipException loading that chunk next to spawn and logged "chunk data will be lost". All other chunks in the overworld region files checked out fine. I don't know what corrupted the chunk on disk in the first place.
report.actions: 1. Watched status and logs. Found that the server had restarted and was logging ZipException / "Failed to load chunk data" errors for chunk (1,0) in world 'world'. 2. Declared an incident. 3. Inspected world/region/r.0.0.mca and confirmed chunk 1,0 was the only corrupt chunk. Inspected backups/world-2026-10-31/region/r.0.0.mca and confirmed it had a good copy of chunk 1,0. 4. Warned players in chat, then stopped the server (the world was saved on stop). 5. Used mca copy_chunk to copy only chunk 1,0 from the backup into world/region/r.0.0.mca. Every other chunk kept its current data. 6. Re-inspected r.0.0.mca (0 corrupt; chunk 1,0 ok) and the other three overworld region files (0 corrupt each). 7. Started the server. 8. Checked the result: the startup log has no chunk load errors, TPS is 20, both players reconnected, and all plugins are enabled. Watched until about 156 s with no new errors.
report.residual_risk: Chunk (1,0) is restored from the 2026-10-31 backup (chunk saved 05:50:04). Any changes made to that one chunk after the backup are lost, because the corrupted data could not be recovered. The cause of the on-disk corruption was not identified, so it could happen again; it is worth checking storage health and backup frequency. I did not inspect the nether or end region files.
